title: Practicing forgiveness
hookLine: forgiveness is a decision before it's a feeling
tomorrow: why would Jesus tell you to walk out in the middle of worship?

cards: The sorry arrives by text. You type it's fine, delete it, type it again. It isn't fine yet.
Genesis has a scene that starts right about there. Joseph's brothers once sold him as a slave. Years later he runs Egypt for Pharaoh, and he has fed the whole family through a famine.
Then their father Jacob dies, and the brothers panic. Maybe Joseph was only waiting for this. They send word: before he died, your father asked you to forgive us.
Then they come in person and fall down at his feet. And Joseph…

teach.b: Joseph weeps. Genesis gives him tears before it gives him a word. Here's what makes that strange: he had already forgiven them.

teach.h: HE HAD FORGIVEN THEM YEARS BEFORE.
teach.b: Years before, when he first told them who he was, he wept so loudly the Egyptians heard, and he told them not to be grieved or angry with themselves. The decision was made back then.
Now the fear is back, and so are his tears. So he makes the decision again, out loud. Fear not, he tells them.

teach.h: YOU THOUGHT EVIL; GOD TURNED IT TO GOOD.
teach.b: You thought evil against me, but God turned it into good. And he comforts them and speaks kindly to them. Notice what he doesn't do.
He doesn't say it never happened; he names it as evil. Forgiving doesn't rewrite the past. It decides what happens next.
Jesus does the same on the cross, before anyone says sorry at all.
In the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." One to tell a friend tonight: Jesus forgave from the cross with no apology in sight.

Luke says the soldiers went right on casting lots for his clothes, and the rulers went on scoffing. Nothing had been fixed or explained. In both scenes the feelings come and go, like weather over a house.
It comes first, and it holds.

how: Catholics pledge to forgive each time they pray the Our Father (as we forgive those who trespass against us), and confession is a place to bring a hurt they are still working to forgive.

o: pretending that what happened never mattered
waiting until the hurt fades away on its own
choosing to release a debt before the heart agrees

p: dies, and the old fear comes back

s: you have to feel ready before you can forgive
Joseph's tears came back years later, and the decision held. the choice can come before the feeling.
Jesus forgave from the cross before anyone apologized
Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
Joseph told his brothers they never really meant him harm
he said they thought evil against him, and God turned it into good.

games.q: you're Joseph. your father has died, and your brothers bow and ask you to forgive them. you forgave them years ago. what do you do?
o: weep, then tell them again: fear not.
remind them you already forgave them once.
test them first, to see if they've changed.
games.why: Genesis says Joseph wept, then comforted them and spoke kindly. he made the old decision new, out loud.

practice: Let one name come to mind, someone you're still sore at, not the deepest wound. Say it quietly, out loud: I decide to forgive, and then the name. The feeling may lag behind, the way Joseph's tears came back years later.
If you pray, you can add the words from the cross: Father, forgive them.

wordCard.voice: Practicing forgiveness. Choosing to release a debt, and choosing it again when the hurt returns, even before the heart agrees. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: forgive, let go. the word Luke gives Jesus on the cross: Father, forgive them.

carryVoice: Your line: decide first. Joseph wept all over again, and his choice still held. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
